title: Client runtime compatibility & graceful degradation policy for streaming, pagination, and retries
creator: Priya Singh
description: PRD: Define a cross-language (Python/TypeScript/Go) compatibility policy and concrete client behavior for streaming responses, paginated endpoints, and retry semantics so that Redwood customers experience predictable, debuggable behavior during runtime changes and model/service rollouts. This ticket captures requirements, acceptance criteria, migration guidance, and rollout plan for the Client SDK Stability Initiative.
background: We observe customer confusion and production incidents when server-side changes (e.g., switching stream framing, introducing continuation cursors, or adjusting retryable error codes) change the observed client behavior. Different SDKs have subtle semantic differences (stream chunking, iterator lifetimes, backoff jitter) that complicate migrations between runtime versions. The goal is to reduce surprise and provide a documented compatibility path.
goals: Create a single source of truth for runtime compatibility guarantees that applies across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs.
Define deterministic graceful-degradation behavior for streaming endpoints (e.g., partial results, last-chunk markers, resumable cursors).
Standardize pagination primitives and cursor semantics so clients can rely on stable iterator patterns and transition smoothly to server-driven cursors.
Unify retry policy defaults and provide explicit hooks for deterministic idempotency and backoff control.
Ship clear acceptance criteria, migration guides, and automated tests that validate cross-language behavior.
Keep breaking changes behind explicit major-version flags and provide runtime compatibility headers that SDKs surface to customers for introspection.
non_goals: This ticket is not a redesign of the entire SDK surface or replacement of existing higher-level helper functions.
It will not change transport (HTTP -> gRPC) decisions; transport improvements will be tracked in separate ENG tickets.
No UI/Console work for exposing compatibility flags is included here (separate product work).
requirements: A compatibility contract document that enumerates semantics for: streaming chunk boundaries, end-of-stream markers, resumable stream cursors, paginated cursor/offset behaviors, and retry classification (idempotent vs non-idempotent).
SDK behavior must be explicit: streaming APIs must expose a deterministic end-of-stream error vs normal close; partial-finalization events must be signaled consistently across languages.
Pagination helpers must provide: a standard iterator abstraction, an explicit Cursor type (opaque string), a deterministic has_more boolean, and a stable next_cursor transition pattern.

Retry defaults: SDKs should default to a conservative retry policy (max_attempts=3, base_backoff=200ms, max_backoff=2s, jitter=full) for idempotent requests and no automatic retries for non-idempotent requests unless client opts-in via explicit idempotency token.

Streaming resumption: server will support resumable cursors for long-running streams where feasible; SDKs must expose resume() that accepts a server-provided resume_token and replays cached context safely.
Compatibility headers: API responses must include X-Redwood-Compat-Version and X-Redwood-Feature-Flags; SDKs must surface these in standard response metadata objects.
Language-specific expectations: Python async iterator, TS async iterable, and Go channel/iterator ergonomics must behave equivalently in normal, partial, and error terminal cases.
Automated cross-language e2e tests that run against a compatibility test harness to validate streaming/pagination/retry permutations.
Detailed error taxonomy and mapping to SDK exceptions for Python/TS/Go with stable error codes and guidance for user-handled vs auto-handled cases.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility contract doc published in Confluence and approved by Eng + SDK leads (review signoffs captured).
Three language SDKs implement the documented streaming end-of-stream semantics and surface resume tokens in identical metadata shapes (tests assert equality of metadata keys).
Pagination helpers across SDKs expose Cursor type and next_cursor transition documented in example snippets; migration script for legacy clients included.
Retry defaults implemented and validated by a fault-injection test suite that simulates transient vs terminal failures.

A compatibility test harness with >= 30 deterministic test cases (stream partials, abrupt disconnects, resume flows, pagination corner cases, retryable vs non-retryable errors) passing in CI for all SDKs.
Migration guide published with code diffs for common upgrade paths and a deprecation schedule for any newly deprecated behaviors (minimum 3 months notice).
Telemetry emitted for compatibility header exposure and resume-token usage; dashboards created in Datadog/Grafana with basic alerting on resume failures.
No customer-facing incidents attributable to incompatible streaming/pagination changes for 6 weeks after rollout across canary customers.
migration_guidance: For streaming: prefer using the SDK-provided resume() flow. If you previously relied on low-level chunk boundaries, update to check for 'final_chunk' metadata key; examples included below.
For pagination: replace offset-based consumption with Cursor-aware iterators. Add a short migration snippet in each SDK: old for-loop -> new cursor-iterator.
For retries: audit usage of non-idempotent endpoints and explicitly add an idempotency_token when retries are desired.
Provide a feature-flagged compatibility shim in SDKs that can be enabled to revert to legacy framing for urgent customer rollbacks during early rollout windows.
api_examples:
Python streaming (async):
async for chunk in client.responses.stream_generation(prompt="Hello"):
    if chunk.metadata.get('final_chunk'):
        handle_final(chunk)
Pagination (all languages): example uses .iterate_pages() helper that yields pages with fields {items, next_cursor, has_more}.
Retry (pseudo): SDK default retries for idempotent calls: client.with_retries(max_attempts=3, backoff_ms=200).
telemetry_and_metrics: Emit traces with span attribute redwood.compat_version and redwood.resume_token_id
Create Datadog dashboard: Stream resume success rate, Pagination cursor errors, Retry backoff escalations
Define alert: resume failure rate > 3% for 15m triggers P1 investigation.
rollout_plan: Week 0: Publish compatibility contract and design doc; SDK leads review and sign off.
Week 1-2: Implement SDK shims and compatibility headers in API (ENG collaboration).
Week 3: Run cross-language e2e harness against staging; iterate on fixes.
Week 4: Start a progressive rollout with 5% traffic canary and opt-in early access customers; observe metrics.
Week 5-6: Expand rollout to 50% then 100% if no regressions; publish migration guide and deprecation schedule.
Contingency: activate legacy-framing feature flag if incompatibilities surface, followed by emergency patch planning.
